title: Forget the Skis: UCI Snow Bike World Championships Return to France in 2027
content:
There’s no off-season for rainbow stripes! The UCI has announced that the 2027 Snow Bike World Championships will return to Châtel, France, on January 23, 2027. This marks the fourth consecutive year the Portes du Soleil ski resort has hosted the event. Expect to see familiar discipline names, with riders competing for world titles in Super-G and dual slalom. However, the conditions and terrain will be very different.

Both men’s and women’s championships will take place on the same day. Giving riders two chances to leave Châtel with a rainbow jersey.

What Exactly Is Snow Bike Racing?

It’s not Fat Biking, so let me clear that up now. But if you’ve ever taken your mountain bike down a ski slope and wondered how fast you could go before things got out of hand, you already know the general idea.

The UCI’s snow bike discipline borrows heavily from alpine ski racing. But you’re trading dirt and rocks for snow, ice, and some particularly interesting traction management.

The Super-G is a single timed downhill run through a series of gates, same as on the dirt. It still rewards outright speed and precise cornering, but now throws in the need to find grip on snow.

The dual slalom is a little more familiar to mountain bike folks. Two riders race head-to-head on parallel courses through tightly spaced gates, advancing through elimination rounds until a winner is crowned.

As you might imagine, tire choice and setup matter a lot. Riders aim for enough grip to hold a fast line without sacrificing speed. It presents a slightly different set of problems than your typical downhill mountain bike race.

Can Anyone Beat Lisa Baumann?

Switzerland’s Lisa Baumann has been particularly dominant since the discipline received its own UCI World Championships in 2024.

Baumann won both titles in 2026. She became the first rider to successfully defend a Super-G World Championship title while taking her third consecutive dual slalom title.

On the men’s side, France’s Pierre Thévenard reclaimed the Super-G title he originally won in 2024. A fellow Frenchman, Vincent Tupin, took the dual slalom title.

France swept both men’s podiums in 2026, so the international field should have plenty of motivation heading into January.

So are you ready ot watch? Check out the schedule below!

2027 UCI Snow Bike World Championships Schedule

Saturday, January 23, 2027

  • 10:00 AM: Women’s and men’s Super-G
  • 12:00 PM: Super-G podium ceremonies
  • 5:00 PM: Women’s and men’s dual slalom
  • 7:00 PM: Dual slalom podium ceremonies

All times are local (CET).

The Super-G will take place on the L’Aity and Linga slopes. The evening dual slalom will be contested on the Linga slope.

It’s also a big year for non-snow cycling in Haute-Savoie. It will play host to the larger 2027 UCI Cycling World Championships later in the year.

Snow bike racing is still a relatively young UCI discipline. But four consecutive World Championships suggest it’s found a home in Châtel. It’ll be interesting to see whether more World Cup downhill regulars start working snow bike racing into their winter schedules. Because the call for a rainbow jersey is just as powerful in winter as in summer.

Either way, it’s considerably more entertaining than watching someone ride a smart trainer in January.
